alternatives.reason_rejected: A half-shipped point release with no review is worse than a complete breakdown; the deletion defect has been live since 2.x and one more session does not change the field's exposure materially

context: Wrote the 2.16.1 / plugin 1.34.1 TDD breakdown (docs/plans/2026-09-05-2.16.1-implementation.md): 7 tasks with full test and implementation code; execution deferred to a fresh session per the per-release convention (context at 81%)
rationale: The plan's own convention is one fresh session per release breakdown; the breakdown carries complete test and implementation code (ingest retention keyed on the filename stem for every file, records/**/*.tmp gitignore entry, argv dispatch extracted to src/cli/dispatch.ts with an unknown-word exit-2 guard, validate-records as a pure validateRecordsTree + CLI wrapper), the release steps at true cost (bump-plugin-version.sh patch → 1.34.1, npm version 2.16.1, pre-tag review in worktree isolation, tag push, both-scope plugin update), and the repro tests are preserved under the gitignored .planning/2.16.1-repro-tests/ so the executing session re-derives from executed evidence, not prose.
summary: Deferred 2.16.1 implementation to a fresh session and shipped its full TDD breakdown instead, rather than starting the code in this session at 81% context
